questions.prompt: Which prompt is a stronger shot prompt?

options.text: "A sneaker, nice, cool, high quality, trending, best photo, very detailed, perfect colours."
options.explanation: These words don't say anything about the shot. The model still guesses the setting, light and angle.

options.text: "A photograph of a white sneaker on a concrete step, soft side light, low-angle, 4:5."
options.explanation: Right. It gives the subject, setting, light, camera and format.

questions.prompt: You want a street with no cars. What does Google's guide suggest?

options.text: Write "no cars, no trucks, no buses, no bikes" in the prompt.
options.explanation: The Gemini API docs suggest describing the scene you want instead of listing the things you don't want.

options.text: Write "an empty, deserted street with no signs of traffic".
options.explanation: Right. This is the example Google gives of a semantic negative prompt.

options.text: Write "empty street" and add "no cars, no cars" at the end.
options.explanation: Google's tip is to describe the scene positively, not to repeat a ban.

questions.prompt: An image needs a short headline inside it. What should you do with the words the model draws?

options.text: Check every letter. OpenAI's docs say the model can still struggle with text placement.
options.explanation: Right. Proof-read any words in the picture.

options.text: Nothing. Text is the easiest part for image models, so a quick glance is enough. It is enough to look at the preview once.
options.explanation: OpenAI's docs list text rendering as a limitation.

options.text: Shorten the prompt so the model has less to think about and fewer words to draw.
options.explanation: A shorter prompt gives less direction and does not fix text errors.
